docs.text: "Speaking to one another with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord." Ephesians 5:19

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Welcome to the Jesus' Disciples Song Book, a growing collection of Christ-centered songs, hymns, worship songs, and spiritual melodies.

This online songbook has been created to help believers worship God, meditate on biblical truths, and preserve spiritually rich songs for future generations.

docs.title: 🌿 Purpose
docs.text:
This songbook seeks to:

  • Glorify the Lord Jesus Christ
  • Preserve spiritually rich songs
  • Encourage personal devotion
  • Strengthen congregational worship
  • Help believers learn the truths of God's Word through song

docs.title: 📜 Featured Scripture
docs.text:
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.

Colossians 3:16

docs.title: 🙏 A Prayer
docs.text:
May every song in this collection draw hearts closer to the Lord Jesus Christ and help believers worship Him in spirit and in truth.

"To Him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen." Ephesians 3:21

docs.title: He Walked Where I Walked
docs.text:
Song: He Walked Where I Walked | God With Us

Copyright Information: Graham Kendrick. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: He walked where I walked He stood where I stand He felt what I feel He understands He knows my frailty Shared my humanity Tempted in every way Yet without sin

God with us So close to us God with us Emmanuel Emmanuel

One of a hated race Stung by the prejudice Suffering injustice Yet He forgives Wept for my wasted years Paid for my wickedness He died in my place That I might live

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rziwfk7_hbU

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 He walked where I walked He stood where I stand He felt what I feel He understands He knows my frailty Shared my humanity Tempted in every way Yet without sin

Meaning: This beautiful opening powerfully declares the truth of the Incarnation. Jesus did not remain distant — He entered fully into our human experience. He walked the same roads, stood in the same struggles, felt the same emotions, and faced the same temptations we face. Yet, unlike us, He remained completely without sin. He knows our weakness from the inside and still understands us perfectly with compassion.

Chorus God with us So close to us God with us Emmanuel Emmanuel

Meaning: The chorus celebrates the heart of the Christmas message and the gospel itself — “God with us.” Jesus is not a far-off God but Emmanuel, God who came near. He is so close that He shares our humanity completely. This truth brings comfort, intimacy, and awe: the holy God chose to dwell among us and remain with us.

Stanza 2 One of a hated race Stung by the prejudice Suffering injustice Yet He forgives Wept for my wasted years Paid for my wickedness He died in my place That I might live

Meaning: This stanza highlights the depth of Christ’s love and identification with the marginalized and broken. Jesus was born into a despised people, experienced racism and injustice, yet responded with forgiveness. He wept over our wasted, sinful lives and willingly took our punishment upon Himself. His death was substitutionary — He died in our place so that we might have life. This is the gospel in its most personal and moving form.

Summary of Song This powerful Graham Kendrick song beautifully captures the wonder of the Incarnation and the depth of Christ’s empathy and love. It reminds us that Jesus didn’t stay in heaven — He walked in our shoes, felt our pain, faced our temptations, experienced injustice, and still chose to die in our place. The repeated cry of “God with us… Emmanuel” anchors the song in the glorious truth that God came near. It is a deeply comforting and worshipful song that draws us to marvel at a Saviour who fully understands us and gave everything to bring us life. Perfect for Christmas, communion, or any time we need to remember how close and compassionate our God truly is.

docs.title: Love Divine All Loves Excelling
docs.text:
Song: Love Divine, All Loves Excelling

Copyright Information: Charles Wesley (Lyrics), Public Domain. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: Love divine, all loves excelling, Joy of heaven, to earth come down; Fix in us thy humble dwelling, All thy faithful mercies crown. Jesus, thou art all compassion, Pure, unbounded love thou art; Visit us with thy salvation, Enter every trembling heart.

Breathe, O breathe thy loving Spirit Into every troubled breast; Let us all in thee inherit, Let us find that second rest. Take away our bent to sinning; Alpha and Omega be; End of faith, as its beginning, Set our hearts at liberty.

Come, Almighty to deliver, Let us all thy grace receive; Suddenly return and never, Never more thy temples leave. Thee we would be always blessing, Serve thee as thy hosts above, Pray and praise thee without ceasing, Glory in thy perfect love.

Finish then thy new creation, Pure and spotless let us be; Let us see thy great salvation Perfectly restored in thee. Changed from glory into glory, Till in heaven we take our place, Till we cast our crowns before thee, Lost in wonder, love and praise.

Source: https://youtube.com/watch?v=0iJsZ6QEUbY

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 Love divine, all loves excelling, Joy of heaven, to earth come down; Fix in us thy humble dwelling, All thy faithful mercies crown. Jesus, thou art all compassion, Pure, unbounded love thou art; Visit us with thy salvation, Enter every trembling heart.

Meaning: This opening stanza passionately invites God’s perfect, supreme love (which surpasses all other loves) to come down from heaven and make its home in us. It asks Jesus — the embodiment of pure compassion and infinite love — to enter our fearful hearts, bring salvation, and crown us with His ongoing mercies.

Stanza 2 Breathe, O breathe thy loving Spirit Into every troubled breast; Let us all in thee inherit, Let us find that second rest. Take away our bent to sinning; Alpha and Omega be; End of faith, as its beginning, Set our hearts at liberty.

Meaning: The prayer continues by asking the Holy Spirit to breathe His loving presence into every anxious heart. It seeks the “second rest” (full sanctification or perfect peace in Christ), deliverance from our natural tendency to sin, and true freedom as we experience Jesus as the beginning and end of our faith.

Stanza 3 Come, Almighty to deliver, Let us all thy grace receive; Suddenly return and never, Never more thy temples leave. Thee we would be always blessing, Serve thee as thy hosts above, Pray and praise thee without ceasing, Glory in thy perfect love.

Meaning: This stanza pleads for God’s almighty power to deliver us and for His grace to fill every life. It longs for God’s permanent presence (never leaving His people, who are His temples) so that we can continually worship, serve, pray, and rejoice in His perfect love, just like the angels in heaven.

Stanza 4 Finish then thy new creation, Pure and spotless let us be; Let us see thy great salvation Perfectly restored in thee. Changed from glory into glory, Till in heaven we take our place, Till we cast our crowns before thee, Lost in wonder, love and praise.

Meaning: The final stanza asks God to complete the work of making us holy and spotless — fully restoring His image in us. It expresses the hope of continual transformation from one level of glory to another until we reach heaven, where we will lay our crowns before Him in overwhelming wonder, love, and eternal praise.

Summary of Song This beloved hymn by Charles Wesley is a deep, passionate prayer for God’s perfect love to dwell in us, transform us, and make us holy. It moves from inviting divine love and the Holy Spirit into our hearts, to seeking deliverance from sin, continual worship, and ultimate completion in Christ. With its rich theology and tender longing, the song beautifully captures the journey of Christian sanctification — from initial salvation to full restoration and eternal glory. It is ideal for worship services focused on the Holy Spirit, personal holiness, or deeper intimacy with God.

docs.title: O The Spirit Filled Life
docs.text:
Song: O The Spirit Filled Life

Copyright Information: Christmas Evans, Public Domain. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: O the Spirit filled life; is it thine, is it thine? Is thy soul wholly filled with the Spirit Divine? O thou child of the King, has He fallen on thee? Does He reign in thy soul, so that all men may see The dear Savior’s blest image reflected in thee?

Has He swept through thy soul like the waves of the sea? Does the Spirit of God daily rest upon thee? Does He sweeten thy life, does He keep thee from care? Does He guide thee and bless thee in answer to prayer? Is it joy to be led of the Lord anywhere?

Is His service thy choice, and is sacrifice sweet? Is the doing His will both thy drink and thy meat? Dost thou run at His bidding with glad eager feet?

Has He freed thee from self and from all of thy greed? Dost thou hasten to succor thy brother in need? As a soldier of Christ dost thou hardness endure? Is thy hope in the Lord everlasting and sure? Hast thou patience and meekness, art tender and pure?

O the Spirit filled life may be thine, may be thine, In thy soul evermore the Shekinah may shine; It is thine to live with the tempests all stilled, It is thine with the blessed Holy Ghost to be filled; It is thine, even thine, for thy Lord has so willed.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ib3j6X15gUM

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 O the Spirit filled life; is it thine, is it thine? Is thy soul wholly filled with the Spirit Divine? O thou child of the King, has He fallen on thee? Does He reign in thy soul, so that all men may see The dear Savior’s blest image reflected in thee?

Meaning: The song opens with searching, personal questions that challenge the believer. It asks whether we truly possess a Spirit-filled life — one where the Holy Spirit completely controls and fills the soul. The evidence is whether Christ’s character is visibly reflected in us for others to see.

Stanza 2 Has He swept through thy soul like the waves of the sea? Does the Spirit of God daily rest upon thee? Does He sweeten thy life, does He keep thee from care? Does He guide thee and bless thee in answer to prayer? Is it joy to be led of the Lord anywhere?

Meaning: This stanza describes the powerful and daily effects of the Holy Spirit: like mighty waves cleansing and filling the soul, bringing sweetness, peace, guidance, answered prayer, and joyful willingness to follow God anywhere.

Stanza 3 Is His service thy choice, and is sacrifice sweet? Is the doing His will both thy drink and thy meat? Dost thou run at His bidding with glad eager feet?

Meaning: These lines examine our attitude toward serving God. A Spirit-filled life makes obedience a delight, sacrifice feel sweet, and doing God’s will as satisfying as food and drink, with eager readiness to obey.

Stanza 4 Has He freed thee from self and from all of thy greed? Dost thou hasten to succor thy brother in need? As a soldier of Christ dost thou hardness endure? Is thy hope in the Lord everlasting and sure? Hast thou patience and meekness, art tender and pure?

Meaning: This stanza lists the practical fruits of being filled with the Spirit: freedom from selfishness and greed, quick compassion for others, endurance in hardship, firm hope in God, and the growth of Christ-like qualities such as patience, meekness, tenderness, and purity.

Stanza 5 O the Spirit filled life may be thine, may be thine, In thy soul evermore the Shekinah may shine; It is thine to live with the tempests all stilled, It is thine with the blessed Holy Ghost to be filled; It is thine, even thine, for thy Lord has so willed.

Meaning: The song ends on a strong note of hope and invitation. The Spirit-filled life is available to every believer. God’s glory (“Shekinah”) can shine continually in our hearts, bringing peace amid storms, because the Lord Himself desires and wills this for us.

Summary of Song This classic hymn by Christmas Evans is a probing and encouraging call to experience the fullness of the Holy Spirit. Through a series of honest, self-examining questions, it reveals what a truly Spirit-filled life looks like — marked by God’s presence, victory over self, joyful obedience, Christ-like character, and inner peace. The song moves from challenge to wonderful assurance that this blessed life is available to every child of God who desires it. It is ideal for personal reflection, prayer meetings, or revival services when the church seeks a deeper work of the Holy Spirit.

docs.title: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice
docs.text:
Song: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

Copyright Information: Keith Green. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: To obey is better than sacrifice To obey is better than sacrifice I don't need your money I want your life And I hear you say that I'm coming back soon But you act like I'll never return

Well you speak of grace and my love so sweet How you thrive on milk, but reject My meat And I can't help weeping of how it will be If you keep on ignoring My words

Well you pray to prosper and succeed But your flesh is something I just can't feed

To obey is better than sacrifice I want more than Sunday and Wednesday nights Cause if you can't come to Me every day Then don't bother coming at all La, la, la

To obey is better than sacrifice I want hearts of fire Not your prayers of ice And I'm coming quickly To give back to you According to what you have done According to what you have done According to what you have done

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dk5nU4hYNs0

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 To obey is better than sacrifice To obey is better than sacrifice I don't need your money I want your life And I hear you say that I'm coming back soon But you act like I'll never return

Meaning: The song opens with God’s direct rebuke, quoting the Bible (1 Samuel 15:22). External religious acts or offerings (sacrifice) mean nothing without heartfelt obedience. God desires our whole life and genuine relationship, not empty words or rituals. Many claim to wait for Jesus’ return but live as if He is not coming.

Stanza 2 Well you speak of grace and my love so sweet How you thrive on milk, but reject My meat And I can't help weeping of how it will be If you keep on ignoring My words

Meaning: God confronts superficial believers who talk about His grace and love but refuse deeper spiritual maturity (rejecting the “meat” of His Word for easy “milk”). He weeps over the coming consequences for those who continually ignore His commands.

Stanza 3 Well you pray to prosper and succeed But your flesh is something I just can't feed

Meaning: This short but sharp line addresses self-centered prayers focused only on personal success and comfort. God refuses to indulge the selfish desires of the flesh; He wants transformation, not pampering.

Chorus / Bridge To obey is better than sacrifice I want more than Sunday and Wednesday nights Cause if you can't come to Me every day Then don't bother coming at all La, la, la

Meaning: God demands consistent, daily devotion rather than occasional church attendance. Half-hearted, weekend-only Christianity is unacceptable. The “la la la” mocks empty, insincere worship.

Final Chorus To obey is better than sacrifice I want hearts of fire Not your prayers of ice And I'm coming quickly To give back to you According to what you have done According to what you have done According to what you have done

Meaning: The song closes with a powerful call for passionate, fiery hearts instead of cold, formal prayers. It ends with a solemn warning of Christ’s return and judgment — we will each receive according to our deeds, emphasising the eternal importance of true obedience.

Summary of Song This convicting song by Keith Green is a bold prophetic call from God’s perspective, challenging shallow, hypocritical Christianity. It powerfully reminds believers that God values wholehearted daily obedience far above religious rituals, attendance, or self-serving prayers. With its raw honesty and urgent tone, the song calls for genuine repentance, fiery devotion, and a life fully surrendered to the Lord in preparation for Christ’s return. It is especially impactful for personal reflection, revival meetings, or when the church needs to examine the sincerity of its faith.
